newsitem.title: USA: Case against former Texaco exec delayed.
newsitem.headline: Case against former Texaco exec delayed.

text.p: A federal magistrate Tuesday postponed a preliminary hearing for 30 days in the case against a former Texaco Inc. executive accused of planning to destroy documents in a racial discrimination lawsuit.

Last month, federal prosecutors sought the first extension to provide time for plea negotiations in the case against Richard Lundwall, former senior coordinator for personnel services in White Plains, N.Y.-based Texaco's finance department.
The U.S. attorney's office in Manhattan said it did not file any additional papers in the latest postponement.
The preliminary hearing, which had been set for Wednesday, is now scheduled for Feb. 13 unless a plea bargain is reached.
Lundwall, who was forced into retirement in August as part of staff reductions, is among those who have been punished by Texaco for their role in the alleged scheme.

The incident came to light after Lundwall turned over to plaintiffs' lawyers in the racial discrimination lawsuit the secret tapes he had made of himself and other Texaco officials discussing destroying papers requested in that case.
Plaintiffs lawyers in that lawsuit made transcripts of the tapes public as part of court proceedings.
Texaco has since offered to settle the lawsuit for $176.1 million, and a federal judge is expected to sign the preliminary accord this week. A fairness hearing on the settlement is set for Feb. 27.

Last week, Texaco announced it had fired a top insurance subsidiary executive allegedly involved in the scheme and had permanently suspended all allowable benefits to Lundwall and Robert Ulrich, a retired Texaco treasurer.
